title: A youthful cluster
caption: The globular cluster NGC 1783 in the Large Magellanic Cloud, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 1783 · constellation Dorado · about 150000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: NGC 1783's symmetry and the crowding of its stars toward the center stand out plainly in this image from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys. Both are typical features of globular clusters, tightly packed, self-gravitating star groups that circle galaxies like satellites.

Among the largest globulars in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a small galaxy that orbits our own, NGC 1783 lies nearly 160 000 light-years from Earth. John Herschel first observed it in 1835. It weighs in at around 170 000 Suns.

From the colors and brightnesses of its individual stars, astronomers estimate that NGC 1783 has existed for less than one and a half billion years, which is very young for a globular. It is thought to have had at least two bursts of star formation, 50 to 100 million years apart. The idea is that supernovae from the first massive stars blew away the leftover gas, which gentler, longer-lived stars later replenished before a second round began.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.29 x 1.93 arcminutes) and distance (150000 light years), the frame spans roughly 144 × 84 light-years. Its light set out about 150,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys, using blue, visible and near-infrared filters. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: The near-infrared light is invisible to the eye, and Hubble's sharp view separates individual stars in a cluster in another galaxy.

explore: This ebb and flow can repeat a few times, until the remaining gas is thought to be too little to form new stars. The cluster lies in the southern constellation Dorado, and Judy Schmidt entered a version of the image in Hubble's Hidden Treasures competition.
alt: A symmetrical globular cluster with stars concentrated toward the center.
